imperial.expected: Onions and shallots are among the most useful crops in the kitchen garden, providing fresh bulbs, salads, pickles and winter stores. Spring-planted sets offer a simple start; seed gives a wider choice of colours, sizes and seasonal types. Shallot bulbs usually divide into clusters, while overwintered onions provide earlier harvests. All need clean, fertile ground and careful drying for storage, but differ in timing and bolting risk.
imperial.proposed: Grow onions and shallots for fresh bulbs, salads, pickles and winter stores. Spring sets offer a simple start; seed gives more choice of colour, size and season. Shallots usually form clusters; overwintered onions crop earlier. All need clean, fertile ground and thorough drying for storage. Timings and bolting risk vary.
imperial.reason: Tighter wording preserves the original advice or variety distinctions.
